comment: Disk tree for the DYNAMIC-USERLAND GATE (run.sh dynamic).
Differs from manifest.json in exactly three intentional ways.
1. /sbin/launchd is the static exec-runner work/init_exec, which
execve()s the dylib-linked /bin/echo.  That is the point of the gate:
manifest.json's PID 1 execs nothing, so the standard boot cannot
observe dyld, the libSystem closure or a dylib main().
2. BOTH EFI paths -- System/Library/CoreServices/BOOT.EFI and
EFI/BOOT/BOOTX64.EFI -- are the fresh source-built apple-free loader
work/efi/BOOTX64.EFI, not the gitignored assets/ copies, which went
stale and caused the pre-kernel failure in BOOT-PLAN sec. 15.10.
3. /usr/lib/dyld is the freshly source-built MH_DYLINKER at
../../Libraries/dyld/dyld/dyld, not the assets/ copy, which is a
DYLIB (988088 bytes).  The kernel rejects a DYLIB as the dynamic
linker before dyld runs at all, with OS_REASON_EXEC /
EXEC_EXIT_REASON_BAD_MACHO -- see BOOT-PLAN sec. 15.6, where the
throwaway probe that proved this staging path was left in work/ and
never promoted here.  The built image is filetype MH_DYLINKER with
0 LC_LOAD_DYLIB and, as of 2026-10-01, 0 undefined symbols and 0
chained BIND fixups -- the bootstrap-dylinker invariant that a
dylinker is mapped before anything is bound, so it must carry zero
imports.  See BOOT-PLAN sec. 15.7.
Any other divergence between the two trees is a bug in this file, not
a feature.
The 'init_exec' marker makes mkimage.py select work/init_exec.
WHY A REPO-RELATIVE PATH AND NOT THE SDK ONE. mkimage.py resolves a
non-absolute "file" against tools/bootlab (os.path.join(HERE, p)), so
../../Libraries/dyld/dyld/dyld is the repo build product and needs no
absolute path.  The same bytes are also installed to
$RAVYN_SDKROOT/usr/lib/dyld by Libraries/dyld/dyld/makefile, but that
copy lives outside the repo and moves with the build directory, so a
manifest naming it would pin a machine-specific path.  Either may be
relinked at any time; the image is what records which one ran, via the
<out>.digests sidecar, which is hashed from bytes read back OUT of the
finished image rather than from these source files.
NOT STAGED FROM THE BUILD, DELIBERATELY. /usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib and
the usr/lib/system/ glob still come from assets/.  The built
libSystem.B.dylib reexports libsystem_pwdgrp.dylib and
libsystem_termcap.dylib, neither of which is staged under assets/, and
mkimage.py hardcodes the glob source to assets/ (asset_prefix), so the
build products are unreachable by this manifest as written.  Widening
that is a separate change with its own closure analysis; see the
offline audit for the measured 17-identical / 12-divergent /
17-absent split across assets/usr/lib/system/.
